purpose: An editorial map separating current public-UI reproductions from retained earlier calculation evidence. Each current capture receipt identifies its actual runtime, workflow release and native case exports; separately authored CLI/SDK clients retain their own configurations.
scope: All named people and numerical businesses are fictional Hermod-authored examples. A common presentation does not establish semantic equivalence; mappings retain candidate meanings, requirements, source scope, coverage and conclusion limits.

comparisons.question: Which supplied complete repairs meet the recorded operating requirements?
comparisons.fixed: The four supplied repairs, qualifications, other availability, earlier work, full 6–10 p.m. assignment, flat fees and $856 remaining-payroll limit. Compare without ranking.
comparisons.changed: Only the recorded relief-window end changes from 10 p.m. to 8 p.m.
comparisons.established: Full availability: relief and coordinated repairs pass. Short availability: the relief repair fails AVAILABILITY; the coordinated repair remains feasible. Neither calculation establishes a preference.
comparisons.limit: Covers the four supplied repairs. A single passing option without a ranking policy is not a demonstrated policy-based preference. Calculation obtains no employee agreement.

comparisons.question: Which feasible repair does the declared comparison favor?
comparisons.fixed: Full relief availability and all mandatory facts. Identical feasible alternatives and the same current feasibility evaluation.
comparisons.changed: Only comparisonPriority changes from stability to cost.
comparisons.established: Stability prefers relief ($836 payroll, $180 additional expense, one changed position). Cost prefers the coordinated repair ($736 payroll, $80 additional expense, three changed positions). Retained baseline $656; remaining-payroll limit $856.
comparisons.limit: These are ordered policies, not a monetary measure of fairness or employee inconvenience. Both policies have unique preferred outcomes here; no tied result is demonstrated.

comparisons.question: Which complete deployments preserve floor coverage?
comparisons.fixed: Seven qualified staff before callouts, a four-person minimum inside and the same supplied deployments, timing and expense requirements.
comparisons.changed: Only unavailable staff changes from two to three: available staff fall from five to four.
comparisons.established: With five available, hold and send one pass. With four available, only hold passes. Applying the change invalidates the old answer before recalculation.
comparisons.limit: The current public capture reproduces the original staffing comparison. Its native fixture retains the actor name Sam; Alex is the site narrative character. Inspection and calculation perform no dispatch or authorization.

comparisons.question: What additional response would cover the commitment?
comparisons.fixed: One-person deployment expense $200, retained contribution $40 per genuinely additional guest, no separately recorded discount loss.
comparisons.changed: No forecast or response measurement is added. This is a conditional calculation at the recorded basis.
comparisons.established: Five genuinely additional guests cover the expense. Six produce the first positive whole-guest result under these assumptions.
comparisons.limit: A threshold is not predicted attendance, expected profit, an incremental causal effect, or a profit ranking. Operating feasibility and authority remain separate.

comparisons.question: Which unreserved shipment proposal meets the commitment under cost-first priority?
comparisons.fixed: The same shipment, arrangements, readiness, scope, permissions, $5,000 expense limit and cost-first policy.
comparisons.changed: The current review/action-ready time advances from 480 to 690 minutes (8 a.m. to 11:30 a.m.).
comparisons.established: Direct at $4,000 Friday noon is preferred before its 11 a.m. booking cutoff. After that cutoff, Consolidated at $5,000 Thursday evening is preferred while its noon cutoff remains available.
comparisons.limit: This scenario concerns making a new reservation. A cutoff passing does not cancel an existing reservation; actual bookings need their own scoped records. It is separate from the registration-and-verification example.

comparisons.question: Which arrangements remain supported across the admitted registration situations?
comparisons.fixed: The first-shipment registration-and-verification workflow 1.8.0 in the public application and its recorded uncertainty.
comparisons.changed: This is a separate case, not a changed input to the booking-window scenario.
comparisons.established: Backup at $6,000 is supported while the $4,000 Direct arrangement is unsupported across the admitted registration situations.
comparisons.limit: Unsupported under admitted uncertainty does not establish that the ship point is known to be unregistered. Its hypothetical verification comparison is separate from the Python model-based learning example.

comparisons.question: Could a timely check improve on reserving Backup now?
comparisons.fixed: The same supplied features and numerical proposal; the modeled available responses and $6,000 reserve-now alternative.
comparisons.changed: Fee-only comparison: $200 to $2,500. Separate duration-only comparison: 120 to 390 minutes, putting the usable result at 3 p.m. instead of before the noon action cutoff. Scenario IDs/titles label the cases.
comparisons.established: Timely $200 check: expected complete expense $5,772.96. Higher fee: $8,072.96. Late result cannot support the noon response. A check must be compared as a complete investigation-and-response alternative.
comparisons.limit: Expected cost is not a realized quote or guaranteed saving. Numerical premises require domain support. This is not the separate registration UI example and does not compute the First Principles essays’ illustrative entropy or soft-target utility.
